name: How much contingency should a luxury custom home budget include?

mainEntity.name: How big should the contingency be for a high-end custom home in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: How big should the contingency be for a high-end custom home in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Contingency is one of the most misunderstood parts of a custom home budget. It is not extra spending money; it is a reserve for unknown conditions, coordination issues, and scope changes that are common in high-end construction. The amount needed depends on how complete the plans are, how difficult the site is, and how much is still undecided. Luxury homes generally need a larger contingency than standard homes because the finishes, systems, and site conditions are more complex. Owners should also distinguish contingency from allowances, since those solve different problems. A strong budget presentation explains both clearly and shows what triggers each one so the project can absorb surprises without derailing the plan.
acceptedAnswer.description: A contingency is a reserve for unknowns, design revisions, site surprises, and price changes. Luxury custom homes usually need a meaningful contingency because complex sites, finish upgrades, and owner changes can quickly add cost.
